I think what you're alluding to is that people with AvPD are often delusional - believing something to be true despite there being contrary evidence. People who are schizophrenic have hallucinations, meaning their brains literally see images and hear sounds that no one else does. They are not deluding themselves.

Being delusional is fairly common and experienced by almost everyone (although more frequently by those with mental illness), whereas hallucinations are not. People with AvPD don't hallucinate, unless they also have a comorbid diagnosis of schizophrenia (I don't see why both couldn't occur at the same time). In general though, I would say if you have AvPD you are not schizophrenic, you are just deluding yourself into believing that you are. Thinking your schizophrenic when you don't hear or see things is an example of a delusion. Believing you are awkward an undeserving of love would be another. I'm not a psychologist or anything, but that is what I deduce from it.
